crm_notes: Lead: ByteHaven Tools — small devtool startup building a context-rich code assistant embedded in their web IDE. Inbound from organic search + blog; signed up for hosted API trial. Key ask: support very long context windows (40k tokens typical per session) and predictable per-dev latency for interactive completions. -- CTO Aaron: "We need delta streaming and chunked context support; users will paste 10-20 files often." -- Product: prefers Node and Rust SDKs; asked if there are official client libraries or sample wrappers (they saw JS SDK in docs but want typed examples). Rate limits: heavy burstiness during office hours (15–30 concurrent dev sessions, short bursts of ~50 reqs/min). Cost sensitivity: early-stage, runway ~18 months — wants rough cost per 1M tokens and guidance on batching + caching to keep unit costs low. Security: requires SSO for admin console, audit logs for user actions, and optional KMS key management for customer data. POC plan: spin up a small hosted flow using Redwood hosted API, run live in their beta IDE for 2 weeks, evaluate latency and token costs, then decide on committed capacity or continue self-serve. Notes are intentionally terse — typical CRM fragments: "need SDK examples", "streaming vs chunking tradeoffs", "what happens when context > model limit? fallback?", "can we pin to a model variant?". Referenced artifacts: pricing deck, security FAQ, Fireflies transcript (FF-20260303-9876).
